Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. Our compliance team asked me to follow up with two specific items for the questionnaire so we can close the security review: 

1) Key material / keystore policy: for hosted API customers, does Redwood hold any customer encryption keys? If so, what is the rotation policy and proof we can use for audits? Do you offer BYOK or HSM-backed keys per-tenant?

2) Regional erasure SLAs: if we request a tenant-level purge for EU data, what are your operational SLAs for deletion from (a) live stores, (b) disaster recovery snapshots, and (c) cold backups? Please call out any exceptions (e.g., legal holds) and whether deletions are synchronous or eventual.

Attached is our short RFI doc (we'll need the answers in the format we can paste into our questionnaire). Can you also point me to any evidence artifacts (attestations / runbooks) we can share with auditors?

Appreciate it — Anna

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear asks. Below are concise answers you can paste into the questionnaire; I've included a brief operational note and flagged evidence items.

1) Keystore policy / keys we hold
- Redwood does NOT retain customer-managed plaintext keys for hosted API tenants by default. For standard hosted customers we manage envelope keys (KMS-wrapped) for service functionality.
- BYOK / HSM: We support customer-provided master keys via integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault. When BYOK is enabled the master key never leaves the customer's KMS; Redwood receives short-lived, KMS-wrapped key material on demand.
- Rotation: For Redwood-managed envelope keys we rotate the wrapping key material every 90 days and maintain a rotation log that records key IDs, timestamps, and operator actions. For BYOK the customer controls rotation cadence; Redwood honors new key versions on receipt.

Operational evidence: keystore rotation diagram and rotation log excerpt (attached: redwood_keystore_rotation.png).

2) Regional erasure SLAs (hosted API)
- Live stores (primary region): standard tenant-level purge completes within 48 hours for typical datasets; the purge job is deterministic and returns a deletion confirmation token once complete.
- Snapshots / DR: snapshot removal is initiated immediately after live-store purge; full removal from DR snapshots may take up to 7 days depending on snapshot lifecycle and replication windows. We mark snapshots as expunged and include a timebound attestation in the confirmation.
- Cold backups / archives: cold backups are on a 30–90 day rolling retention depending on the storage class; explicit purge requests initiate a retention override and removal, which completes within 30 days.
- Exceptions: legal holds, subpoena, or cross-tenant forensics requests will pause erasure until release. Customers can flag holds via legal@redwood.ai with valid documentation.
- Deletion model: live-store deletion is synchronous (you receive a confirmation token). Snapshot and backup removals are asynchronous with timestamps and audit log entries.

Operational evidence: sample deletion confirmation format + sample audit log entry (we'll provide a redacted runbook snippet and log excerpt in the follow-up).

Irene / Kim — adding you for any regional nuances (EU data residency / encryption-at-rest evidentiary items).

Next steps: Anna, I'll follow up with the runbook snippets and the small evidence pack. If you need a faster SLA for snapshots/cold backup removal we can discuss a dedicated contract amendment for accelerated purge windows.

Best,
Mateo
